assumptions: A qualified subcontractor can perform required field work without the founder becoming the regulated technical signatory.
Target sites have enough asset value that an independent evidence pack can be economical relative to a direct repair or replacement decision.
Asset owners can lawfully provide sufficient inverter, maintenance, warranty, and inspection data for a useful assessment.
The stated capital and founder-time limits remain binding during the pilot.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid pilots showing accepted price, full travel and subcontractor contribution margin, repeatable access to usable system histories, and written acceptance criteria or referral commitments from at least one portfolio owner, lender, insurer, buyer, or repowering channel would support a higher score.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The proposal identifies a credible gap between fragmented operating and inspection data and the decision evidence needed at a repair, sale, refinance, warranty, or repowering trigger. The fixed-scope, independent pack is a useful synthesis, although it resembles a productized version of existing technical due diligence rather than a uniquely new mechanism.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: PV degradation and failure can affect energy yield and asset decisions, but the packet provides no Polish purchase commitment, observed budget, or quantified loss from inadequate evidence. Small-site owners may rationally prefer a repair or replacement quote over a separate diagnostic purchase.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Deposits, fixed scopes, and subcontracted fieldwork make a capital-light service plausible, but the 2,500-7,500 PLN price and 45-65% contribution-margin target are hypotheses. Travel, calibrated testing, specialist review, insurance, referral share, and exception handling could consume the proposed margin, while repeat demand is mainly event-driven.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Aging small-commercial rooftop systems form a plausible emerging segment, and a consenting family-firm pilot offers a concrete learning beachhead. The number, timing, and asset value of Polish systems reaching a decision where this report is economical remain unestablished.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Independence from replacement-equipment sales and a small fixed-price scope are useful positioning choices, but engineering consultancies, OEM teams, and installers can provide or bundle comparable work. No exclusive channel, accepted standard, or narrow segment in which the venture could dominate is yet controlled.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Portfolio reviews, post-repair verification, more equipment cohorts, and additional transaction types provide logical expansion paths. Meaningful scale would still require portfolio contracts and standardized acceptance, because one-off regional audits alone remain operationally constrained.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Normalized failure and realized-yield outcomes could eventually improve cohort models, but obtaining complete permissioned histories will be difficult and the initial report workflow is readily imitated. Nonexclusive, at-will referral access offers little durable protection.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The founder's analytical fit, renewable-sector familiarity, and lawful pilot route create a modest starting advantage. Those advantages do not supply accreditation, proprietary data, lender acceptance, or exclusive distribution, and the family channel is explicitly replaceable.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Installed PV fleets will age and increasingly encounter failures and repowering choices, so the direction is credible. The thesis is framed around a 2033 operating state, and the packet does not establish that the targeted Polish small-commercial cohort has reached sufficient transaction density today.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Installer service calls and asset-decision intermediaries expose customers at an appropriate trigger, and the family-firm relationship can support a bounded pilot. Beyond that route, all referral agreements are proposed, nonexclusive, and dependent on partners who may prefer to retain or monetize the customer themselves.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A bounded service pilot is executable within the stated capital and time envelope, especially with delegated field collection. Reliability across OEM data, professional-qualification requirements, safety and financial liability, field density, and quality control make dependable scaling materially harder.

highest_value_structural_change: Narrow the initial product to one high-value trigger and one homogeneous system class, then secure a portfolio owner or finance counterparty that contractually accepts a defined evidence standard and an accredited review partner before building broader referral distribution.
main_structural_strength: The offer sits at a specific high-consequence asset decision and turns fragmented operational, warranty, visual, and thermal evidence into a portable independent deliverable, with a lawful route to test the workflow.
primary_score_limiter: There is no evidence that a defined Polish payer will buy the proposed standardized pack or that lenders, insurers, buyers, and warranty counterparties will accept it without bespoke accredited engineering work.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Many small systems may be cheaper to repair or replace from an installer quote, while institutional users may require accredited bespoke reports; either condition would remove the standardized pack's price and margin advantage.
